With emotion, as we wait for the exit-poll results of the 2025 presidential election, I am showing you a new icon painted in our workshop:

«The Holy Trinity in a single body» – a study after a rare icon that I admired at the ASTRA National Museum Complex in Sibiu. Its author is believed to be Ioan Costea, second half of the 19th century.

About the icon:

The Holy Trinity in one body is depicted through the image of the Saviour Jesus Christ blessing with His right hand and holding in His left hand the sceptre, the symbol of almighty power. The Saviour is shown floating on a chain of clouds. His three-faced countenance is framed by a triangular halo, a symbol of the Trinity. On each side, two cherubim keep watch over Him.

The icon is not available. On a new order, I will gladly paint this special theme again.

3d90a232d3b3:
«The Resurrection of the Lord Jesus» (a study after a 19th-century icon, Savu Moga)

⊹The theme, treated in the Western manner, shows Jesus holding the banner of victory, standing on the clouds. The soldiers who guarded His tomb look up at Him. The two Myrrh-bearing Women complete the picture, together with a praying angel. The soldiers wear hussar uniforms: red and green tunics with gold braid, blue trousers, red boots and helmets with red crowns, gilded mounts and plumes. The soldier on the left wears a shirt of gilded chain mail and holds a curved sabre above his head. The composition is set within a border. (Description: the National Museum of the Romanian Peasant)

⊹The icon is not available. If you would like an icon on glass on this theme (or any other iconographic theme), contact me and we will settle the details.

⊹May the Feast of the Resurrection be blessed with joy in every soul and in every home!
e116f5f748b0:
«Jesus Christ surrounded by the Holy Apostles» – icon on glass, painted in our workshop.
Model: workshop in Lancrăm, Sebeș Valley, second half of the 19th century.

Today, the Lancrăm icon that inspired us belongs to the parish of Grințieș, just 10 km from the border of the former Austro-Hungarian Empire.
The church was built in 1793–1794 by Transylvanian woodworkers who had already settled in the area.
The Habsburg Empire was forcing Romanians to accept the Greek Catholic rite and to leave the Orthodox faith.
And so, real communities of Transylvanians formed in Moldavia, bringing with them their traditions, their dress, their faith and their icons on glass, unique in the world.

About the icon:
Jesus Christ is painted in the centre, shown frontally, in a high bust. The image of Jesus is set within a border with a “rope motif”. Each saint is framed in a medallion: Saint John the Evangelist and the Holy Apostles Peter, Paul, Matthew, Luke, Simon, Philip, James, Bartholomew, Thomas, Andrew and Mark.

The icon is not available. If you would like an icon on this theme, contact me.
fd4b33dd200d:
«Saint Ephraim the New» – icon on glass

• Excerpts from «Efrem cel Nou, dăruitor al credinței și al înnoirii lăuntrice» (Ephraim the New, giver of faith and of inner renewal), Sophia Publishing, 2015:

• From the age of 14, Saint Ephraim the New lived in the Monastery of the Annunciation near Nea Makri, where he was also martyred.

• In 1416 the Ottomans occupied the region of Attica. In 1424, attacking the monastery, the Ottomans beheaded all the monks, but Saint Ephraim escaped unharmed, because he was in a cave where he used to pray.

• The following year, the pagans attacked the monastery again and captured Saint Ephraim as well. On 14 September 1425, when the Saint turned 41, he was taken captive. For eight and a half months he was subjected to terrible torture in the very courtyard of his monastery, to make him renounce the Christian faith.

• The pagans, seeing that Saint Ephraim bore the torture bravely, nailed him to a mulberry tree, hung him upside down, pierced his body with iron nails and finally thrust a burning piece of wood into his belly.

• Saint Ephraim departed to the Lord on 5 May, at the age of 42.
161dfd3f2fbf:
The Annunciation – 25 March

▫︎ The Annunciation, the day the Archangel Gabriel met the Mother of God.
"Who could clearly describe the emotion of the Archangel Gabriel, sent to announce to Mary (an earthly woman living a heavenly life) that she would conceive and give birth to the Creator of heaven and earth?" Source: Doxologia.ro

▫︎ The feast icon on glass (model: Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century) shows at its centre the scene of the Annunciation to the Mother of God by the Archangel Gabriel: that she would give birth, as a man, to the Son of God. The iconographic scene is framed by a simple border that separates it from 10 panels with icons of saints and feasts: the Virgin Mary, the Coronation of the Virgin, Saints John the Baptist, Nicholas, Basil, George, Constantine and Helen, Demetrius, Gregory and Peter.
572ea7ade0a9:
8 March – Women's Day

To celebrate «Women's Day», I have chosen a few words about «the Mother of God – woman par excellence” and one of the icons on glass painted in our workshop, depicting «the Coronation of the Mother of God».

His Eminence Calinic, Archbishop of Suceava and Rădăuți:
“The Mother of God was blessed by God with an unimaginable dignity. She is woman par excellence.
The being who gives birth to Christ is not just any woman, but woman par excellence, blessed by God with an unimaginable dignity.
And Jesus is not the son of Joseph the Righteous, but of Mary alone, being conceived “of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 1:20). This link between the virgin conception and the work of redeeming mankind is also captured in the verses saying that “she will bear a Son” (Matthew 1:21) and that “He will save His people from their sins” (Matthew 1:21).”

Under the protection of the Mother of God: happy Women's Day, ladies!

· A new personalised icon: «The Table of Paradise» or «The Heavenly Feast» – Icon on glass (model: Nicula, 19th century).

· The iconographic theme divides the space of the composition into five rhombus-shaped fields, separated by bands decorated with the «rope» motif.

· The central rhombus holds an oversized floral motif, which is repeated in the triangular fields next to the five rhombuses.

· Leaning on the sides of the middle rhombus are the four rhombuses showing the guests taking part in the heavenly feast. The Mother of God with the Child and Jesus Christ blessing are always in the upper rhombuses; the others hold other saints, in this case Saint Basil the Great and Saint John the Baptist.

· For a personalised order, you propose the saints you wish to have depicted in the two lower rhombuses.
